newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ports of Auckland crews to strike.
newsitem.headline: Ports of Auckland crews to strike.

text.p: Strike action by tug and pilot boat crews at Auckland ports is set to start on Wednesday night, the New Zealand Press Association reported,
Talks on Tuesday failed to resolve the pay dispute between the ports company and the two unions representing the small but critical group of workers.
The unions said they were presented with a lower pay offer and threatened with job losses if they stopped work.
They gave notice a fortnight ago of the strike action which will start with half-day stoppages from 11 p.m. to 11 a.m. NZT in the first week and escalate into a total stoppage next week.

Without tugs and pilots, ships cannot move in and out of the ports. Spokesmen for the unions said the company presented a lower pay offer today than the one that had been rejected previously by the 40 staff.

John McLeod, of the Merchant Service Guild, said ports company chief executive Geoff Vazey told them that if they went out, the company would eventually find ways of quitting the business of towage and pilotage.
